metadata.title: Does Nvidia have its equivalent of Tim Cook lurking within? - MarketWatch

content.text:
25 min ago
Does Nvidia have its equivalent of Tim Cook lurking within?
Investors can look to Apple if they want to see how a company deals with the loss of a seemingly irreplaceable leader.
"Apple lost Steve Jobs twice, with opposite results," Bryce Coward, the chief investment officer of Meridian Wealth Management, told MarketWatch. "In 1985, the board forced him out with no one ready to carry his vision, and Apple nearly went bankrupt. In 2011, Tim Cook had already run the company during Jobs’s medical leaves."
Nvidia faces an "abrupt and board-driven" shakeup, much like what happened in the early Apple example, he noted. "But the business looks more like 2011" as Nvidia has "an entrenched platform."
